:knowledge-point/_canonical-example.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y = vx$  (where $v=v(x)$) to rewrite the given first-order homogeneous ODE 

$$
\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}    =   \cos \left( \frac {y} {x} \right)
$$

as a separable ODE in $v$ and $x.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
With $y = vx$ (where $v = v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging that into the differential equation and separating variables, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(v) \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(v)-v \\ (\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(v)-v})\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3{y}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}+y{x}^{2}}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3{y}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}+y{x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{3(vx)^{3}}{x(vx)^{2}+(vx){x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{3{v}^{3}{x}^{3}}{v{x}^{3}(v+1)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{3{v}^{3}\cancel{{x}^{3}}}{v\cancel{{x}^{3}}(v+1)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3{v}^{2}}{v+1}-v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3{v}^{2}}{v+1}-\frac{v(v+1)}{v+1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3{v}^{2}-{v}^{2}-v}{v+1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2{v}^{2}-v}{v+1} \\ (\frac{v+1}{2{v}^{2}-v})\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{y})+\frac{y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{y})+\frac{y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{vx})+\frac{vx}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{1}{v})+v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{1}{v}) \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{1}{v})} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{1}{v})\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}})+\frac{3y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}})+\frac{3y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{v}^{2}{x}^{2}})+\frac{3vx}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{1}{{v}^{2}})+3v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{1}{{v}^{2}})+2v \\ (\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{1}{{v}^{2}})+2v})\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2}}{{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2}}{{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{x}^{2}-x(vx)+(vx)^{2}}{(vx)^{2}+{x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{x}^{2}(1-v+{v}^{2})}{{x}^{2}({v}^{2}+1)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{1-v+{v}^{2}}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1-v+{v}^{2}}{{v}^{2}+1}-v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1-v+{v}^{2}-{v}^{3}-v}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1-2v+{v}^{2}-{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{{v}^{2}+1}{1-2v+{v}^{2}-{v}^{3}}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}-{y}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}+2y{x}^{2}}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}-{y}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}+2y{x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{x}^{3}+x(vx)^{2}-(vx)^{3}}{x(vx)^{2}+2(vx){x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{x}^{3}(1+{v}^{2}-{v}^{3})}{{x}^{3}({v}^{2}+2v)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{1+{v}^{2}-{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}+2v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1+{v}^{2}-{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}+2v}-v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1+{v}^{2}-{v}^{3}-{v}^{3}-2{v}^{2}}{{v}^{2}+2v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1-{v}^{2}-2{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}+2v} \\ \frac{{v}^{2}+2v}{1-{v}^{2}-2{v}^{3}}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{x})}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{x})} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & ={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{vx}{x})} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & ={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡v}-v \\ \frac{1}{{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡v}-v}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Transforming a Homogeneous Differential Equation into a Separable Equation Using a Substitution

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{y}{x}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{x}).
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{y}{x}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{vx}{x}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{vx}{x}) \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v-2\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡v}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{2}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
